channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Appeals Court Keeps Venezuelan Deportation Protections Frozen for Now
item.description: A federal appeals court in San Francisco has kept deportation protections for hundreds of thousands of Venezuelans suspended, hours after the Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene in the case.

item.title: Senate Rejects Bid to Rein In Trump's War Powers on Iran
item.description: The United States Senate has voted down a resolution that would have told the president to halt the fighting with Iran unless Congress approved it, in the chamber's first vote on the conflict since the midterm elections.

item.title: Burnham Says Europe Is Ready to Join Talks to End Russia's War in Ukraine
item.description: Britain's prime minister says Europe is ready to enter negotiations to end Russia's war in Ukraine, after a meeting of Kyiv's allies that also brought the American mediators trying to broker a settlement to the table.

item.title: Aid Group Warns Gaza's Children Face Dangers Seen Nowhere Else After Three Years of War
item.description: After three years of war, children in Gaza are living with dangers found nowhere else on Earth, Save the Children has warned in a new global report, with at least 20,000 children killed and survivors facing repeated displacement, hunger and the loss of schooling and health care.

item.title: Three French Officers Face Prison as Court Nears Verdict in 2020 Beating of Black Music Producer
item.description: A Paris court is due to deliver its verdict on Friday in the trial of three police officers accused of beating Black music producer Michel Zecler at his studio in November 2020, after prosecutors asked for prison terms of four to six years.

item.title: Anthropic Hits $2 Trillion in Record Nasdaq Debut
item.description: Anthropic's shares soared on their first day of trading on Thursday, pushing the maker of the Claude chatbot to a valuation of about $2 trillion in the biggest stock market debut ever recorded.

item.title: Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah Reach Deal as Federal Troops Prepare to Enter Militia Stronghold
item.description: Iraq's government has reached a compromise with the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah militia over control of its stronghold south of Baghdad, with federal troops due to move into the area on Friday morning under a joint command.

item.title: Putin Vows 'Far More Painful' Response After Third Strike on Crimean Bridge
item.description: President Vladimir Putin has vowed a response 'far more painful' than Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, dropping any idea of a truce on energy and Black Sea attacks after the crossing was hit for a third time in a week.

item.title: European Commission Confirms AI-Tool Cyberattack Disrupted Its Systems for Over Ten Days
item.description: The European Commission has confirmed it was targeted by a cyber campaign carried out with the help of artificial intelligence tools, disrupting staff systems for more than ten days.

item.title: Pentagon Strategist Walked Out of NATO Meeting After Rebuking Ukraine Over Deep Strikes
item.description: The Pentagon's top policy official left a meeting with European allies in Brussels early after criticising Ukraine for its long-range strikes inside Russia, according to a report that has alarmed several allied governments.

item.title: Trump Official Suggested Venezuela Take Part of Guyana's Essequibo, Sources Say
item.description: A senior official in Donald Trump's administration raised the idea of Guyana handing Venezuela partial control of the Essequibo region, a vast territory that covers about two-thirds of Guyana, according to a report published on Thursday.

item.title: JPMorgan Chase Says Customer Names and Emails May Have Been Exposed in Vendor Cyberattack
item.description: JPMorgan Chase has said some customer names and email addresses may have been exposed after hackers attacked outside companies that provide services to the bank.

item.title: South Korea's Top Court Orders Retrial for Ex-PM Han Over Martial Law Role
item.description: South Korea's Supreme Court has overturned former prime minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence over his role in the December 2024 martial law crisis and ordered a retrial, in the latest twist in the fallout from the six-hour decree.

item.title: Denmark Approves Greenland Security Deal With US in Unanimous Vote
item.description: Denmark's parliament has unanimously approved a security agreement with the United States covering Greenland, a deal meant to end months of tension over the Arctic island's future after repeated threats from Washington to take control of it.

item.title: Somalia Orders UAE Ambassador Out Within 72 Hours, Citing 'Open Invasion'
item.description: Somalia has ordered the ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to leave the country within 72 hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the Gulf state of violating its sovereignty in what Mogadishu called an open invasion.

item.title: 'Gaza Syndrome': Film Examines the Trauma Soldiers Carry Home From Gaza
item.description: A new documentary follows Israeli soldiers home from Gaza and asks what their nightmares, panic and grief mean when the people who bore the heaviest cost of the war are almost entirely absent from their accounts.

item.title: UK-EU Talks Go Down to the Wire Before Friday Summit
item.description: Talks between Britain and the European Union are going down to the wire ahead of a summit in Brussels on Friday, with negotiators still racing to close a deal on food, energy and a youth mobility scheme.

item.title: COP31 Draft Drops All Mention of Fossil Fuels as Climate Talks Near Deadline
item.description: Climate negotiators in Antalya have published a revised draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels at all, stripping out the phaseout language that divided nearly 200 countries as the summit heads for its Friday deadline.

item.title: Under-17 World Cup Kicks Off in Qatar Without the USA
item.description: The Under-17 World Cup has kicked off in Qatar with 48 teams, after the United States withdrew its side over security concerns and was replaced by the Dominican Republic.

item.title: US Consortium Wins Kenya Critical Minerals Tender Over Chinese Rivals
item.description: A consortium of American firms has won the tender to develop a critical minerals project at Mrima Hill in Kenya, beating Chinese and Australian rivals for a site reported to hold deposits worth more than $60 billion.

item.title: Mosque Set on Fire in Northern Israel as Politicians Blame Incitement
item.description: A mosque in northern Israel was set on fire early on Thursday in a suspected arson attack, prompting opposition politicians to blame anti-Arab incitement by the government of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: US Clashes With Russia and China at UN Over Iran Nuclear Programme
item.description: The United States has clashed with Russia and China at the United Nations Security Council over Iran's nuclear programme, as Washington pushes to keep sanctions on Tehran in force while the war over Iran continues.

item.title: Yunus Ancestral Home Set on Fire as Bangladesh Unrest Deepens Ahead of Lockdown
item.description: Attackers torched the ancestral home of former Bangladesh leader Muhammad Yunus in the port city of Chattogram late on Wednesday night, police said, as political unrest spread across the country ahead of a nationwide shutdown.

item.title: Florida Pastor Convicted in Miami Over Plot to Kill Haiti's President Jovenel Moise
item.description: A federal jury in Miami has convicted Florida pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon on all eight charges arising from the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moise, after a trial that ran for nearly eight weeks.

item.title: Israel Ends One-Day Tank Raid Across Gaza Ceasefire Line as Main Road Reopens
item.description: Israel's military says it has finished a one-day tank operation in central Gaza, the most serious ground incursion across the ceasefire line since the truce that halted major fighting more than a year ago.

item.title: Trump Says There Are Signs Iran Is Turning to Chemical and Biological Weapons, but Offers No Evidence
item.description: Donald Trump has said there are signs Iran is exploring chemical and biological weapons after its nuclear programme was damaged, while offering no evidence and playing down the threat to Americans.

item.title: Infantino to Face First Contested FIFA Election as Diallo and Tashima Enter 2027 Race
item.description: World football's governing body has confirmed that Gianni Infantino will face two challengers in next year's presidential election, the first contested vote of his decade in charge, after Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan filed their nominations ahead of the deadline.

item.title: World Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya in Landmark Verdict
item.description: The United Nations' highest court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time it has held a state responsible for the crime in its 80-year history.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Issue Joint Peace Declaration After First-Ever Trilateral Summit
item.description: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin have issued a joint declaration on peace after the first-ever trilateral meeting of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, pledging that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

item.title: Japan Tobacco Books $8.6 Billion Loss After Losing Russian Business
item.description: Japan Tobacco expects to book a loss of about 1.38 trillion yen after losing control of its Russian business, pushing the cigarette maker to a full-year loss in the biggest corporate fallout yet from Moscow's seizure of foreign assets.
